details.effects: Law cord-bend@1 keeps both items and lengths; the join is a relation. w = 2 ply diameters, a = mean w; each centreline = standing part + path in the bend + tail. Round 1 bends both to their cord-knot@1 bend limit and picks the bight that leaves both trial grips, else longer standing parts. Bight radius rB = max(limit, a), opened 0.02 m (or other w) to pass; path pi rB + 4 x other w. The other end passes up through it, round both legs at rW = max(its limit, a) and under itself: path = bight w + 2 max(0, 2rB - 2(rW - a)) + 2 pi rW + own w. Tails get 0.02 m + w; a standing part under a 0.02 m pinch is a measured shortfall. Dressing seats both arcs; slack is split between tail and standing part. Retention: friction mu 0.3 (reed; other fibers unsupported), contact angles pi a/rB and 2 pi a/rW; a tail holds while 2 mu e^(mu angle) >= 1, else up to 2 mu x 5 N / (e^(-mu angle) - 2 mu). Records extension, creep, strand damage above half that force, a slip parting the cords or a break into two owned fragments.
